source.title: Exploring Representations and Interventions in Time Series Foundation Models
source.authors: Michał Wiliński; Mononito Goswami; Willa Potosnak; Nina Zukowska; Artur Dubrawski

record.tranche_reason: The paper analyzes time-series representations and concept separability, but does not test superposition, capacity pressure, polysemanticity, SAE features, or what is superposed. Its results concern a related but different representation question.
record.gate_note: The paper reports CKA similarities and pruning outcomes, but these do not measure feature overlap or superposition. Its linear-probing findings on synthetic time-series concepts are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version. Steering results are intentionally induced interventions and do not establish naturally occurring superposition.
record.test_reason: The study probes, prunes and steers time-series foundation models (MOMENT, Chronos, Moirai) using CKA, linear probes with LDR, and steering vectors. It cites Toy Models of Superposition only in related work. It never measures feature overlap, capacity allocation, polysemantic neurons, SAE features, or feature dimensionality. Its linear-separability results concern whether a few hand-built synthetic concepts are linearly decodable. That is a related construct, not superposition. Steering is a deliberate intervention.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that larger TSFMs learn block-wise redundant representations that can be pruned with little accuracy loss. They also conclude that intuitive concepts (periodicity, trend) are linearly represented at specific layers and tokens, and that steering matrices built from these directions can shift predictions toward chosen concepts. They draw no conclusions about superposition.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses CKA, linear probes, and activation steering to study time-series foundation models; it does not reproduce the original toy-model superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Concept separability varies across layers and patches. For the separate steering experiments, the authors report that applying interventions across all tokens is needed for the intended output, and that effective steering strength differs between Chronos and MOMENT.

fits_no_version.finding: In MOMENT-Large, synthetic time-series concepts (pattern, trend, periodicity) are linearly separable only at specific layers and patches. Trend is localized to the initial and final patches, and no amplitude location was found.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Intuitive time-series concepts are linearly represented in TSFMs, with layer- and token-dependent localization.

fits_no_version.finding: Larger TSFMs show block-like high-CKA redundancy across layers. Pruning these blocks cuts model size by up to about 52% with small accuracy loss in imputation and forecasting, but larger degradation in anomaly detection.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Large TSFMs store redundant representations across contiguous layer blocks.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267, 2025
record.problems: The relevant probing results are mainly described qualitatively and illustrated in figures; numerical LDR values and uncertainty estimates are not stated in the text. The experiments concern synthetic time-series concepts in MOMENT-Large, not superposition or language models.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results were included: the CKA similarity and pruning results do not measure the claim’s feature-overlap subject, and the steering outcomes are induced interventions.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, no sparsity sweep, no measure of feature overlap or geometry.
All: no capacity or importance analysis, no neuron-level polysemanticity.
All: polysemantic neurons are not studied.
All: no LLMs, no SAE, no measure of features spread across neurons (TSFMs only).
All: linear directions are assumed for probing and steering, and their dimensionality is never tested against alternatives.

record.verdict_notes: Toy Models of Superposition is cited only alongside related neuron/direction interpretability work. No superposition-relevant results were omitted from the rows.

versions.untested_parts: Whether sparse features outnumber dimensions, overlap as nearly orthogonal directions, or exhibit sparsity-dependent transitions and regular geometry.
Whether capacity pressure causes polysemanticity or allocates dedicated dimensions to important features.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise without capacity pressure, or whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.
Whether LLM features spread across neurons or are recoverable with an SAE dictionary.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical representational units.
Whether the features involved in superposition are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.

rows.subject: MOMENT-Large
rows.operation_detail: Linear probes and LDR assessed separability of constant versus sinusoidal synthetic time-series patterns across layers and patches.
rows.value: Figure only; the text reports that the concepts are linearly separable at specific layers and patches, not uniformly across the model.
rows.note: This measures concept separability and localization, not superposition or feature overlap.
rows.check: The row measures linear separability of constant vs sinusoidal concepts by layer and patch. That says nothing about superposition, so the state relative to any version can't be determined. The value is figure-only (Fig. 7, Fig. 14i), and the LDR is min-max scaled per map, so no absolute value can be read. 'Observed' only describes separability, not a version.

rows.subject: MOMENT-Large
rows.operation_detail: Linear probes and LDR assessed separability of synthetic trend-related concepts across layers and patches.
rows.value: Figure only; the text reports that increasing and decreasing trends can be distinguished by focusing on the initial and final patches.
rows.note: The text does not give a numerical LDR value. This is a result about time-series concept localization, not superposition.
rows.check: Trend-concept localization to the initial and final patches does not bear on any version. The value is figure-only. Fig. 14 panels compare constant vs increasing and sinusoidal vs increasing/decreasing trends.

rows.subject: MOMENT-Large
rows.operation_detail: Probed representations for amplitude-related concepts and assessed their localization.

conditions.value: synthetic time series with varying amplitudes

rows.value: The authors report that they did not identify specific locations where the model distinguishes time series of different amplitudes.
rows.note: The authors suggest input normalization may explain this result. It does not test a superposition claim.
rows.check: Failing to localize amplitude says nothing about superposition. The authors attribute it to input normalization. Fig. 14(iv) is actually labelled sinusoidal vs decreasing trend, so the amplitude result is text-only.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
